message: Unknown action @GET. Did you mean @get?
Datastar reads an action only as @get( with nothing before the parenthesis. With a space the @ reaches the browser, which cannot parse it.
Unknown action @fetch.
Datastar expression: Unexpected end of input
data-on needs a value; without one Datastar raises ValueRequired.
data-on needs a key, e.g. data-on:<event>="expr".
Unknown Datastar attribute data-onn. Did you mean data-on?
data-on-click is Datastar's pre-1.0 syntax, which 1.0 ignores. The key follows a colon: data-on:click.
Unknown modifier __debunce on data-on, which Datastar ignores, so it listens for the event click. Did you mean __debounce?
Datastar reads __debounce.5x as 5 ms. Write __debounce.5ms.
The browser lowercases attribute names, so this reaches Datastar as the event myevent, not myEvent. Write data-on:my-event__case.camel: keys are kebab-case.
This is an aliased Datastar attribute, but the prefix is set to data-. Check streamlord.attributePrefix.
data-text does not take a key.
Datastar reads $my-draft as one signal named my-draft, and nothing here declares it: a key my-draft is the signal $myDraft. For a subtraction write $my - draft, with spaces.
No markup or code in the project defines the signal 'drafty'. Did you mean $draft?
Datastar rewrites $draft in a regular expression into $['draft'], which changes the pattern. Build the pattern with new RegExp('...'): Datastar leaves a quoted string as written.

Datastar splits an expression whose value is used at every ; outside quotes, this one inside brackets too, and returns only what the last piece gives: the value is lost. A function without parameters called at once, (() => { ... })(), is kept whole.
patch is not defined in data-text: Datastar hands an expression patch only in data-on-signal-patch, so here it throws a ReferenceError.

Without a key, data-computed takes an object of functions, such as {total: () => $a + 1}: Datastar declares no signal from this value, and raises ComputedExpectedFunction when it is a string. Name the signal in the key instead: data-computed:total.
data-bind declares the signal $draft, as written, which holds the $ itself, so $draft does not reach it: that reads the signal draft.
data-bind takes a signal name, not an expression.
data-bind takes the signal as a key or as a value, not both; Datastar raises KeyAndValueProvided.
data-indicator needs a signal, as a key or as a value; without one Datastar raises KeyOrValueRequired.
data-indicator takes the signal as a key or as a value, not both; Datastar raises KeyAndValueProvided.
data-indicator tracks the requests this element sends, and nothing on it sends one. Put it on the element whose attribute calls @get, @post, @put, @patch, @delete, @query.
Datastar cuts one / from each end of a string include and takes the rest as the pattern, so /i stays in it and is matched as text, not read as flags. Write the regular expression literal /(?:)/i.
data-ignore takes no value.
data-nonce only works on <html>.
__delay needs a duration such as __delay.500ms or __delay.1s.
data-persist is a Datastar Pro attribute; it needs the Pro bundle.
@clipboard is a Datastar Pro action; it needs the Pro bundle.
